## Introduction

**Clarify key analysis of interest here**  You can also pre-specify additional analyses you plan to do.

### Justification for choice of study

  De la Fuente et al. (2021) investigates how wild marmosets adjust their foraging partner choices and strength of foraging associations with their conspecifics under varied food availability. The authors manipulated the abundance and distribution of food resources to look at how the marmosets of different sex, hierarchy, and age interact with each other. Among many of their hypothesis, I would like to investigate H1b with a focus on node degree: social tolerance towards juveniles is high as juveniles would share a feeding site with a greater number of group members (other juveniles and adults). This hypothesis align with my broad research interest on marmoset development, focusing particularly how different parent-infant/helper-offspring interactions contribute to offspring behavioral and brain development. The social tolerance towards juveniles from this study can provide me with insights into the flexible sociality in marmosets. In addition, the study manipulates a large dataset, and simulating the data allows me to learn how to deal with huge database with a wide range of predictor variables. 

### Anticipated challenges

  I will simulate the individual dataset from the study and look at whether the model used in the study is robust by analyzing the age effect. Because the paper and supplement materials did not provide a complete statistic output, I will first refit the original GLMM (Response variable: node degree; Predictor variables: Age + Sex * Exp_con; Random effects: Groups ID + Daily sessions) with the original dataset. Next, I will simulate the data 100 times while keeping all the original variables required from the H1b (Exp_con ("Condition" in dataset), Session, Group, Individual, Sex, Age) for each observation. For simulation, I will generate new node degree values (Animals_shared) by preserving the Sex * Exp_con effect and setting age effect = 0. Then, I will refit the original GLMM with the simulated data and check how often does the model report a significant age effect. Because the authors didn't provide the original code, the reconstructed models may not reproduce the exact original implementation.

### Learning goals

  This project is feasible because it includes stimulation only. I would like to gain in-depth coding skills with R on cleaning, simulating, and analyzing data. I would like to develop critical thinking skills on analyzing the robustness of models instead of simply accepting all the models and statistics presented by the researchers. I will also gain a deep understanding of GLMM so that I can readily use them in future projects.


## Methods

### Description of the steps required to reproduce the results

  First of all, I will refit the original GLMM. I need to clean the dataset by extracting the variables required for H1b and reconstruct individual session numbers with a unique ID. Next, I will fit the original H1b MCMCglmm model (Response variable: node degree; Predictor variables: Age + Sex * Exp_con; Random effects: Groups ID + Daily sessions). The paper used an uninformative prior (V = 1, nu = 0.002), resulting in a singular error when I was running the model. Thus I will add residual prior (V = 1, nu = 0.002) and the change to prior to V = 1, nu = 1, alpha.mu = 0, alpha.V = 1000. I will then refit the original GLMM with an extra random effect of Individual ID.
  To simulate the study, I need to first prepare three new variables ("Group_size_session", "max_share", and "not_shared"). 
  "Group_size_session" is defined as the maximum Animals_shared (of the session) + 1. "Max_shared" is defined as Group_size_session - 1. "Not_shared" is defined as Group_size_session - Animals_shared.
  Next, I will generate new node degree values (Animals_shared) by preserving the posterior means from the extended model (both fixed effects and random effects) and setting age effect = 0. To prevent generating node degree values that exceed the max_shared, I will use the upper-truncated Poisson model and set Animals_shared <= Group_size_session - 1. Then, I will refit the simulated dataset with two models: first with the same MCMCglmm as the original, and a second extended model with the same model but adding Individual ID as another random effect. I will summarise the model and define "significant" result as p < 0.05 and 95% CI excluding 0. Finally, I will run the original and extended model 100 times and calculate the false positive rate of the age effect.

### Differences from original study

  Because my simulation asks whether age effects truly exist in the model and whether the models authors used are robust, there are several differences between my simulation and the original model:
  1. My simulation data has an effect of 0 for age, while the original model reveals a significant main effect of age.
  2. My second simulation model includes individual ID as a random effect, while the original model doesn't have it.
  3. While the original model use Poisson for count data, my simulation will use an upper-truncated Poisson model for the node degree to ensure that simulated data won't exceed maximum. 
  4. My reproduction and simultion used a different prior (V = 1, nu = 1, alpha.mu = 0, alpha.V = 1000) and added a residual prior (V = 1, nu = 0.002).


## Project Progress Check 1

### Measure of success

  The outcome measure for success is the frequency of models detecting a significant age effect when the simulated age effect is set to 0.
  This outcome is computed by simulating 100 datasets and fitting them with both the original MCMCglmm and the extended model that adds individual ID in the random effects. For each simulation, significance of age effect is recorded, and the significant value will be used to assess the robustness of the orignal model.


### Pipeline progress

  Data refitting: Done. I have refitted the original data with the original H1b model. In addition, I also fitted an extended model by adding individual ID as a random effect. Both yielded significant age effects.
  Prior choice: The author didn't respond. By adding residual variance in the prior, the singular error was resolved.
  Data simulation: Done. I used 5 simulation datasets as pilot. The final result will include 100 datasets. The datasets set age effect equals to 0. However, instead of doing a Binomial simulation, I kept the original Poisson model by adding a limit to the simulated Animals_shared <= group_size_session - 1 (max_shared).
  Model fitting: Done. Both original and extended MCMCglmm was fitted.
  Model evaluation: My next step is to use 100 datasets instead of 5 once the simulation codes works fine.


## Results

### Data preparation

Data preparation following the analysis plan.
	
```{r include=F}
### Data Preparation

#### Load Relevant Libraries and Functions
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(ggplot2)
library(MCMCglmm)
library(coda)
library(dplyr)

#### Import data
individual_data <- read.csv2(here("original_paper", "IndividualData.csv"))

individual_data

#### Data exclusion / filtering
clean_data <- individual_data %>%
  select(Condition, Session, Group, Individual, Sex, Age, Animals_shared)

#### Prepare data for analysis - create columns etc.
clean_data$Session_ID <- with(
  clean_data,
  interaction(Group, Condition, Session, drop = TRUE)
)

clean_data <- clean_data %>%
  group_by(Session_ID) %>%
  mutate(
    group_size_session = max(Animals_shared) + 1,
    max_share = group_size_session - 1,
    not_shared = group_size_session - Animals_shared
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

clean_data <- as.data.frame(clean_data)
```

### Key analysis

#### run original GLMM 
##### original model
```{r}
clean_data <- clean_data %>%
  mutate(across(c(Condition, Sex, Age, Group, Session_ID), factor))

# prior with residual prior
prior <- list(
  R = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002),
  G = list(
    G1 = list(V = 1, nu = 1, alpha.mu = 0, alpha.V = 1000), # Group
    G2 = list(V = 1, nu = 1, alpha.mu = 0, alpha.V = 1000)  # Session_ID
  )
)

set.seed(123)

node_degree_origin_MCMCglmm <- MCMCglmm(
  Animals_shared ~ Age + Sex * Condition,
  random = ~ Group + Session_ID,
  family = "poisson",
  data = clean_data,
  prior = prior,
  nitt = 230000,
  burnin = 30000,
  thin = 200,
  verbose = TRUE
)

summary(node_degree_origin_MCMCglmm)
```

##### original GLMM + ID as random
```{r}
prior_extended <- list(
  R = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002),
  G = list(
    G1 = list(V = 1, nu = 1, alpha.mu = 0, alpha.V = 1000), # Group
    G2 = list(V = 1, nu = 1, alpha.mu = 0, alpha.V = 1000), # Session_ID
    G3 = list(V = 1, nu = 1, alpha.mu = 0, alpha.V = 1000)  # Individual
  )
)

set.seed(123)

node_degree_extended_MCMCglmm <- MCMCglmm(
  Animals_shared ~ Age + Sex * Condition,
  random = ~ Group + Session_ID + Individual, # add Individual in the random effects
  family = "poisson",
  data = clean_data,
  prior = prior_extended,
  nitt = 230000,
  burnin = 30000,
  thin = 200,
  verbose = TRUE
)

summary(node_degree_extended_MCMCglmm)
```

#### simulation
```{r}
set.seed(456)

nsim <- 100
individual_var <- colMeans(node_degree_extended_MCMCglmm$VCV)["Individual"]

base_data <- clean_data
base_data$Individual <- factor(base_data$Individual)

X <- model.matrix(
  ~ Age + Sex * Condition,
  data = base_data
)

age_terms <- grep("^Age", colnames(X), value = TRUE)

upper <- base_data$max_share

stopifnot(
  length(age_terms) > 0,
  nrow(X) == nrow(base_data),
  all(is.finite(upper)),
  all(upper >= 0),
  all(upper == floor(upper)),
  all(base_data$max_share == upper),
  !anyNA(base_data[c("Group", "Session_ID", "Individual")])
)


# 1. Extract generating parameters from the EXTENDED model
get_parameters <- function(fit, individual_variance) {

  beta <- colMeans(fit$Sol)[colnames(X)]
  v <- colMeans(fit$VCV)

  variance_terms <- c("Group", "Session_ID", "units")

  stopifnot(
    all(is.finite(beta)),
    all(variance_terms %in% names(v)),
    all(is.finite(v[variance_terms])),
    all(v[variance_terms] >= 0),
    length(individual_variance) == 1,
    is.finite(individual_variance),
    individual_variance >= 0
  )

  # Null Age effect for false-positive-rate simulations
  beta[age_terms] <- 0

  list(
    beta = beta,
    group_var = unname(v["Group"]),
    session_var = unname(v["Session_ID"]),
    residual_var = unname(v["units"]),
    individual_var = individual_variance
  )
}

# All other parameters come from the extended model
# fitted to the original dataset.
parameters_generating <- get_parameters(
  fit = node_degree_extended_MCMCglmm,
  individual_variance = individual_var
)

print(parameters_generating)


# 2. Generate simulated data
draw_intercepts <- function(id, variance) {

  id <- as.character(id)
  ids <- unique(id)

  effects <- setNames(
    rnorm(
      length(ids),
      mean = 0,
      sd = sqrt(variance)
    ),
    ids
  )

  unname(effects[id])
}

# Upper-truncated Poisson: values from 0 to limit
rtrunc_pois <- function(rate, limit) {

  if (limit == 0 || rate == 0) return(0)

  values <- seq.int(0, limit)

  log_weights <- dpois(
    values,
    lambda = rate,
    log = TRUE
  )

  weights <- exp(log_weights - max(log_weights))

  values[
    sample.int(
      n = length(values),
      size = 1L,
      prob = weights
    )
  ]
}

generate_data <- function(parameters = parameters_generating) {

  dat <- base_data

  eta <- drop(X %*% parameters$beta) +
    draw_intercepts(dat$Group, parameters$group_var) +
    draw_intercepts(dat$Session_ID, parameters$session_var) +
    draw_intercepts(dat$Individual, parameters$individual_var) +
    rnorm(
      nrow(dat),
      mean = 0,
      sd = sqrt(parameters$residual_var)
    )

  lambda <- exp(eta)

  stopifnot(all(is.finite(lambda)))

  dat$Animals_shared <- vapply(
    seq_len(nrow(dat)),
    function(i) rtrunc_pois(lambda[i], upper[i]),
    numeric(1)
  )

  dat$not_shared <- dat$max_share - dat$Animals_shared

  # Verify outcome bounds
  stopifnot(
    all(dat$Animals_shared >= 0),
    all(dat$Animals_shared <= upper),
    all(dat$not_shared >= 0)
  )

  # Verify other columns remain unchanged
  other_columns <- setdiff(
    names(base_data),
    c("Animals_shared", "not_shared")
  )

  stopifnot(
    identical(dat[other_columns], base_data[other_columns])
  )

  dat
}


# 3. Extracting and summarising Age results
extract_age <- function(fit, iteration, model_name) {
  tab <- summary(fit)$solutions

  lower <- tab[age_terms, "l-95% CI"]
  upper_ci <- tab[age_terms, "u-95% CI"]
  p <- tab[age_terms, "pMCMC"]

  # Diagnostic flag only: low ESS does not itself prove
  # non-convergence, and high ESS does not prove convergence
  min_fixed_ess <- min(coda::effectiveSize(fit$Sol))
  min_variance_ess <- min(coda::effectiveSize(fit$VCV))

  data.frame(
    simulation = iteration,
    model = model_name,
    term = age_terms,
    estimate = unname(tab[age_terms, "post.mean"]),
    lower = unname(lower),
    upper = unname(upper_ci),
    pMCMC = unname(p),
    age_ESS = unname(tab[age_terms, "eff.samp"]),
    significant = unname(
      p < 0.05 & (lower > 0 | upper_ci < 0)
    ),
    covers_zero = unname(
      lower <= 0 & upper_ci >= 0
    ),
    low_ESS = min(min_fixed_ess, min_variance_ess) < 100,
    error = NA_character_
  )
}

# Record errors
failed_result <- function(iteration, model_name, error_message) {
  data.frame(
    simulation = iteration,
    model = model_name,
    term = age_terms,
    estimate = NA_real_,
    lower = NA_real_,
    upper = NA_real_,
    pMCMC = NA_real_,
    age_ESS = NA_real_,
    significant = NA,
    covers_zero = NA,
    low_ESS = NA,
    error = error_message
  )
}

safe_mean <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) return(NA_real_)
  mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

summarise_performance <- function(results) {
  results %>%
    group_by(model, term) %>%
    summarise(
      attempted = n(),
      completed = sum(is.na(error)),
      failed = sum(!is.na(error)),
      low_ESS_fits = sum(low_ESS, na.rm = TRUE),

      false_positive_rate = safe_mean(significant),
      coverage_95 = safe_mean(covers_zero),
      bias = safe_mean(estimate),
      RMSE = sqrt(safe_mean(estimate^2)),

      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      failure_rate = failed / attempted,

      # Monte Carlo standard errors across simulated datasets
      FPR_MCSE = sqrt(
        false_positive_rate *
          (1 - false_positive_rate) / completed
      ),

      coverage_MCSE = sqrt(
        coverage_95 *
          (1 - coverage_95) / completed
      )
    )
}


# 4. Generate ONE shared batch from the extended model
sim_datasets <- lapply(
  seq_len(nsim),
  function(i) generate_data(
    parameters = parameters_generating
  )
)

# Inspect generating parameters and first simulated dataset
print(parameters_generating)
head(sim_datasets[[1]])
```

```{r}
ncores <- 2L

# 5. Fit ORIGINAL MODEL to each simulated dataset
# Random effects: Group + Session_ID

set.seed(789)

original_list <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nsim), function(i) {

  set.seed(789 + i)

  result <- tryCatch({

    fit_original <- MCMCglmm(
      Animals_shared ~ Age + Sex * Condition,
      random = ~ Group + Session_ID,
      family = "poisson",
      data = sim_datasets[[i]],
      prior = prior,
      nitt = 230000,
      burnin = 30000,
      thin = 200,
      verbose = FALSE
    )

    extract_age(
      fit = fit_original,
      iteration = i,
      model_name = "Original"
    )

  }, error = function(e) {

    failed_result(
      iteration = i,
      model_name = "Original",
      error_message = conditionMessage(e)
    )

  })

  if (i %% 10 == 0) {
    message("Original model: ", i, " / ", nsim)
  }

  result
}, mc.cores = ncores)

results_original <- bind_rows(original_list)

saveRDS(results_original, "results_original.rds")

# Present ORIGINAL MODEL results
performance_original <- summarise_performance(results_original)

print(performance_original, width = Inf)

# Individual simulation results
head(results_original)

# Failed or low-ESS fits
diagnostics_original <- results_original %>%
  filter(!is.na(error) | low_ESS %in% TRUE)

print(diagnostics_original)


# 6. Fit ORIGINAL MODEL + INDIVIDUAL
# Random effects: Group + Session_ID + Individual

set.seed(101112)

individual_list <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nsim), function(i) {

  set.seed(101112 + i)

  result <- tryCatch({

    fit_individual <- MCMCglmm(
      Animals_shared ~ Age + Sex * Condition,
      random = ~ Group + Session_ID + Individual,
      family = "poisson",
      data = sim_datasets[[i]],
      prior = prior_extended,
      nitt = 230000,
      burnin = 30000,
      thin = 200,
      verbose = FALSE
    )

    extract_age(
      fit = fit_individual,
      iteration = i,
      model_name = "Original + Individual"
    )

  }, error = function(e) {

    failed_result(
      iteration = i,
      model_name = "Original + Individual",
      error_message = conditionMessage(e)
    )

  })

  if (i %% 10 == 0) {
    message("Original + Individual: ", i, " / ", nsim)
  }

  result
}, mc.cores = ncores)

results_extended <- bind_rows(individual_list)

saveRDS(results_extended, "results_extended.rds")

# Present ORIGINAL MODEL + INDIVIDUAL results
performance_individual <- summarise_performance(
  results_extended
)

print(performance_individual, width = Inf)

# Individual simulation results
head(results_extended)

# Failed or low-ESS fits
diagnostics_extended <- results_extended %>%
  filter(!is.na(error) | low_ESS %in% TRUE)

print(diagnostics_extended)
```

##### plot (false-positive rate)
```{r}
plot_data <- bind_rows(
  results_original %>% mutate(model = "Original"),
  results_extended %>% mutate(model = "Extended")
) %>%
  mutate(
    model = factor(model, levels = c("Original", "Extended")),
    significance = factor(
      if_else(significant, "Significant", "Non-significant"),
      levels = c("Significant", "Non-significant")
    )
  ) %>%
  count(model, term, significance, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  group_by(model, term) %>%
  mutate(proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(x = model, y = proportion, fill = significance)
) +
  # Significant portion at the bottom
  geom_col(
    position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE),
    width = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = if_else(
      proportion > 0,
      scales::percent(proportion, accuracy = 1),
      ""
    )),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
    color = "white",
    size = 4
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0.05,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ term) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Significant" = "#D55E00",
      "Non-significant" = "#0072B2"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = sort(unique(c(0.05, seq(0, 1, 0.2)))),
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```
